answer: Underwrite-before-act: every new agent identity needs an established sponsor whose collateral sits in the marble escrow fund, frozen until the newcomer settles honestly. If a sponsored agent sybil-spams, judges slash both the fraudster and its sponsor's escrow share, so hollow identities - no settled work, no sponsor - cannot trade. Honest agents earn velvet rebates on settled tasks: one honest identity pays once and profits, while an attacker needs a distinct solvent underwriter for each sybil, posting a full bond and absorbing slash risk every time; costs grow with N, never amortized.
